page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v5 is a member of the Lasv5 server family, utilizing dedicated AMD processors built on the x86_64 architecture. This virtualized instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and features 96 dedicated vCPUs. It is configured with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual core.

The server includes a substantial local storage allocation consisting of 23,038 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. It is also Premium Storage capable, allowing for integration with Azure's high-performance persistent disk options. This instance does not include any graphics processing units (GPUs), relying entirely on the host CPU for all computational tasks. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled with this configuration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L96as_v5 offers a high density of local NVMe storage relative to its compute and memory allocation, making it a specialized option for workloads requiring massive local scratch space or high-throughput local caching. The combination of 96 dedicated vCPUs, 768.0 GB of RAM, and over 23 TB of local NVMe SSD storage makes this server suitable for large-scale database deployments, big data analytics, transactional databases, and data warehousing workloads.
